description.narrative:
The partnership has presented a very clear and well-though through plan for the competencies that they wish to exchange within three separate areas of health care provision: (1) Internal medicine, with a focus on prevention and treatment of diabetes and hypertension; (2) paediatric care, in particular for infants 0-5 years; and (3) mental health services.
Internal medicine: Through the exchange, MMH will gain knowledge and competence related to the identification and treatment of diabetes and hypertension, both through observation and experiences of MMH participants on exchange at HUH, and through training and skills-transfer from HUH at MMH. Participants from HUH will learn to identify and treat late-stage and complicated cases of these conditions, which are increasing in Norway in particular among immigrant and refugee populations.
Paediatric care: Staff at MMH will gain competence in diagnosing and treating infant sepsis, which is one of the primary causes of infant mortality, while staff at HUH will gain exposure and experience in working with infants with complex symptom presentation at MMH’s paediatric ICU.
Mental health services: Staff in Zanzibar will develop their competence in diagnosing and treating mental health illnesses, and in implementing measures to reduce stigma associated with mental illness. Staff from HUH will learn how patient’s with different cultural and religious backgrounds perceive and respond to mental illness, and how this affects their treatment seeking choices.
In addition to competency development in these three thematic areas, staff from HUH will also (i) learn to identify and treat specific tropical illnesses such as tuberculosis and imported malaria, both of which are increasing in Norway; (ii) learn to work with patients with different cultural and religious backgrounds, and different healthcare expectations; and (iii) gain experience in ethical decision making in resource-constrained settings.
